samples.summary: The #1045 undo-cap data-loss shape is left unfixed on the other multi-block write actions (Tab / indent / outdent / format-painter / multi-block inline style)
samples.evidence:
`withUndoUnit` was added to typing, paste, Enter, page-break, Cmd+Shift+V and Hangul, but the remaining actions that write once per selected block are still unbatched:

- `handleTab` (text-editor.ts:2769-2781) — `saveSnapshot()` then `forEachBlockInSelection(... this.doc.setBlockType(...))`, one store write per list item.
- `handleIndent` (2814-2828) and `handleOutdent` (2835-2851) — same shape, `setBlockType` / `applyBlockStyle` per block.
- `pasteFormat` (543-546) — `saveSnapshot()` then `applyStyleToSelection`, which fans out per block.
- `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:438-442) loops `visitRangeSlices` calling `this.store.applyStyle(...)` once per block slice; `EditorAPI.applyStyle`/`clearInlineFormatting` reach it via `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:1261). (Contrast `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`, which uses the batched `applyStyles`.)

On `YorkieDocStore` each of those writes is its own `doc.update()` and therefore its own undo entry, and `withUndoUnit`'s own doc comment states the failure mode: the stack is capped at 50 (`YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH`) and `pushUndo` shifts the oldest entry off. Indenting, outdenting, Tab-ing, or bolding a select-all over ~100 paragraphs therefore still produces ~100 units, overflows the cap, and drops entries permanently — the same unrecoverable loss the change exists to remove, on paths a user reaches with one keystroke.
searchedFor: grep 'this.saveSnapshot()|withUndoUnit(' in packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts (enumerated all 30 snapshot sites vs the 8 withUndoUnit sites)

samples.summary: A transient share-link revalidation failure now tears down the live editing session
samples.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` was changed from a resolve-once `useEffect` to `useQuery({ refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS, refetchOnWindowFocus: true, staleTime: 0, retry: 1 })`, and the render guard is `if (!token || error || !resolved)`. In react-query a *background refetch* failure sets `error` while `data` is retained, so after two consecutive failures (retry: 1) the component renders the "Link unavailable" screen even though a perfectly good `resolved` is in hand. That unmounts `SharedDocumentInner`, and with it the Yorkie `DocumentProvider`, the docs/slides/notes view and the editor — mid-typing, on any 5xx or CORS/proxy blip from `/share-links/resolve`. The previous code could not do this: `resolved` was set once and never invalidated. The safe shape is to keep rendering while `data` exists and only evict on an authoritative negative (e.g. 401/404), i.e. gate on `error && !resolved` plus an explicit revoked/expired response.

samples.summary: NotesView now remounts on `readOnly` but never releases the store's `doc.subscribe`, unlike the docs and slides views
samples.evidence: `readOnly` was added to the effect deps (notes-view.tsx:167) so an `editor` → `viewer` downgrade rebuilds the editor and constructs a second `YorkieNoteStore`. `YorkieNoteStore`'s constructor registers `doc.subscribe(...)` and discards the returned unsubscribe (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:143-147), and the class exposes no `dispose()`. The cleanup at notes-view.tsx:150-155 only calls `editor.dispose()` and nulls the refs, so every remount leaves another dead store subscribed to the shared Yorkie document, its `captureHistorySelection()` firing on every local undo/redo for the lifetime of the page and retaining the store and its closure. The same hazard is explicitly fixed for docs in this diff (`store.dispose()` at docs-view.tsx:574) and already handled for slides (`store.dispose()` at slides-view.tsx:1216) — notes is the one that got the dependency without the release.

samples.summary: The Hangul-commit undo unit is opened without the `saveSnapshot()` its own contract requires, so undo restores the post-edit caret
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s doc comment (text-editor.ts:3838-3849) states the rule: "`saveSnapshot()` must be called before opening a unit, never inside one" — because on `YorkieDocStore` `saveSnapshot` is what flushes the *pre-edit* caret/selection into presence via `setCursorForHistory` (editor.ts:2538-2551), and that is what Yorkie records as the reverse of the change. The commit branch of `applyHangulResult` (5907-5913) opens a unit around `deleteSelection()` + `docInsertText()` with no `saveSnapshot()` anywhere above it — contrast the sibling `result.composing` branch at 5924, which does call it. So the one undo of a Hangul syllable typed over a selection restores the text but leaves the caret/selection wherever the edit ended, and no `setCursorForHistory` is recorded for that unit at all.
searchedFor: read editor.ts:2519-2559 (saveSnapshot closure passed to TextEditor)

samples.summary: `batch()` now performs three extra whole-document JSON passes on every keystroke in MemDocStore hosts
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit` routes every typing/Enter/paste/delete action through `DocStore.batch()`, and `MemDocStore.batch()` (memory.ts:256-289) does `cloneDocument(this.doc)` + `JSON.stringify(beforeClone)` + `JSON.stringify(top)` up front and `cloneDocument(this.doc)` + `JSON.stringify(...)` again in the `finally`. Combined with `snapshot()`'s own `cloneDocument`, a single character typed goes from one whole-document `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` to roughly four whole-document serializations — and `deleteSelection()` opens its own (nested, so cheap) unit on top. That is fine for a slides text box but scales with document size for the other MemDocStore hosts (the docs demo app, the visual harness), where it is a per-keystroke O(document) cost that did not exist before this change.

samples.summary: Checkpoint adoption is decided by `JSON.stringify` equality, so it is sensitive to key *order*, not just value
samples.evidence: `const adopted = top !== undefined && JSON.stringify(top) === beforeJson;` compares two independently produced serializations. `cloneDocument` normalizes `block.style` on both sides, but nothing normalizes key order for `pageSetup`, `tableData`, or `inline.style` — and several mutators rebuild those objects by spread (`applyCellStyle`'s `{ ...cell.style, ...cleared }`, `applyBlockStyle`'s `normalizeBlockStyle({ ...block.style, ...style })`). A write between the `snapshot()` and the `batch()` that leaves every value equal but re-orders keys makes adoption (and, in the `finally`, `wroteNothing`) report a difference, so the batch pushes a second checkpoint holding the identical state — the dead Cmd+Z the adoption logic exists to prevent. Failure direction is benign (a no-op undo step, never lost data), but the comparison is doing structural equality with a serializer that does not promise it.

samples.summary: A disposed `getStore()` handle still throws from `setPageSetup` where every other member has become a silent no-op
samples.evidence: `pageSetupGuardedStore`'s `get` returns `guardedSetPageSetup` unconditionally (editor.ts:3311) and never consults the revoked target for that key. That function only checks `readOnly`, then runs `assertUsablePageSetup(setup)` (3303) before delegating to the now-inert `revocableStore.setPageSetup`. So after `dispose()` a stale holder calling `getStore().setPageSetup(badSetup)` gets a thrown error, while the same holder calling `insertText`/`deleteBlock` gets a quiet no-op — and the read-only handle's documented contract is that a refused write is a silent no-op precisely so a viewer's screen does not break. Reordering the disposed check ahead of `assertUsablePageSetup` (or reading `isDisposed` here) would make the two agree.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree: handleTab (text-editor.ts:2769-2781), handleIndent (2814-2828) and handleOutdent (2835-2851) each call saveSnapshot() and then write once per selected block via forEachBlockInSelection -> doc.setBlockType/applyBlockStyle, with no withUndoUnit/doc.batch. pasteFormat (543-546) -> applyStyleToSelection (3587) -> Doc.applyInlineStyle (model/document.ts:438-443) fans out one store.applyStyle per block slice, also unbatched; the toolbar path reaches the same loop via applyStyleImpl (view/editor.ts:1261) while stepSelectionFontSizeImpl (editor.ts:1373) uses the batched applyStyles, exactly the asymmetry claimed. The only withUndoUnit call sites are text-editor.ts:835, 1020, 1552, 2664, 2687, 2727, 3875, 4275, 5910 — none on these paths, and no enclosing batch exists at the keydown dispatch (text-editor.ts:1139-1170) or in the frontend docs wiring. The consequence is real: YorkieDocStore.withUpdate opens a standalone doc.update per write outside a batch (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2972-2980) and the undo stack is capped at 50 with the oldest entry shifted off (yorkie-doc-store.ts:570, 589-593), so a select-all Tab/indent/bold over ~100 blocks produces ~100 units and silently drops history. The repo's own design doc concedes the gap (docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:313-321, issue #1048) and even understates it by claiming the keyboard handlers are covered. No counterexample found anywhere I searched.

finding.summary: A transient share-link revalidation failure now tears down the live editing session
finding.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` was changed from a resolve-once `useEffect` to `useQuery({ refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS, refetchOnWindowFocus: true, staleTime: 0, retry: 1 })`, and the render guard is `if (!token || error || !resolved)`. In react-query a *background refetch* failure sets `error` while `data` is retained, so after two consecutive failures (retry: 1) the component renders the "Link unavailable" screen even though a perfectly good `resolved` is in hand. That unmounts `SharedDocumentInner`, and with it the Yorkie `DocumentProvider`, the docs/slides/notes view and the editor — mid-typing, on any 5xx or CORS/proxy blip from `/share-links/resolve`. The previous code could not do this: `resolved` was set once and never invalidated. The safe shape is to keep rendering while `data` exists and only evict on an authoritative negative (e.g. 401/404), i.e. gate on `error && !resolved` plus an explicit revoked/expired response.

verdict.reason: The code matches the finding precisely. `SharedDocumentByToken` polls `resolveShareLink` via `useQuery` with `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` (60s), `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`, `staleTime: 0`, `retry: 1` (shared-document.tsx:1107-1119), and the render guard `if (!token || error || !resolved)` (line 1125) short-circuits to the "Link unavailable" screen (line 1132) whenever `error` is truthy, regardless of whether valid `resolved` data is retained. With @tanstack/react-query ^5.74.4 (packages/frontend/package.json:56) a failed background refetch sets `error` while keeping `data`, so this state is reachable. `resolveShareLink` (api/share-links.ts:99-109) uses bare `fetch` + `assertOk`, so transient network/CORS/5xx failures throw identically to authoritative revocation — there is no distinction between a blip and a revoked link. The preceding `isLoading` guard (line 1121) only covers first load, not refetches, and the app uses a default `new QueryClient()` with no `throwOnError`/retry overrides (App.tsx:88,93), so no guard elsewhere prevents this. When it fires, the success branch at line 1139 unmounts `SharedDocumentInner`, tearing down `YorkieProvider`/`CollabDocumentProvider` and the editor layouts (lines 1040-1077) mid-editing. Real, reachable in normal use, and blocking under the correctness rubric (breaks a core flow / risks unsynced local state).

finding.summary: `dispose()`'s neuter cannot stop the in-flight clipboard paste it claims to close — `EditorAPI.paste()` resumes after `await navigator.clipboard.read()` and writes through the disposed TextEditor
finding.evidence: The new doc comment on `isDisposed` and the comment inside `dispose()` name "a clipboard read" as the case disposal revokes. But neutering replaces `api.paste` only for *future* calls; a call already suspended at `await navigator.clipboard.read()` (editor.ts:3979) resumes in its own closure and reaches `textEditor.pasteContent({ html, text })` (editor.ts:3997, and the `readText()` fallback at 4005). `textEditor` is a `const` (editor.ts:2503) that `dispose()` never nulls — it only calls `textEditor?.dispose()` — and `TextEditor.pasteContent` (text-editor.ts:1659) checks `this.readOnly` and `this.pasting` but NOT `this.disposed`, unlike the other two resuming writes which do (`deferPaste`, text-editor.ts:1609; `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`, text-editor.ts:4261, whose comment even asserts "this is the only one that resumes"). Consequence in exactly the scenario the delta describes: an `editor`→`viewer` downgrade on `/shared/:token` disposes this editor and remounts a read-only one over the SAME Yorkie document (docs-view.tsx:565/590), so the stale paste lands CRDT content into the document a viewer is now supposed to only read, and into a document the disposed editor no longer renders. Fix: check `this.disposed` in `pasteContent`, or re-check a captured `disposed` flag after each await in `api.paste`.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim is false: `TextEditor.pasteContent` DOES check `this.disposed`. text-editor.ts:1671 is `if (this.disposed) return;`, placed ahead of the `readOnly` (1673) and `pasting` (1677) checks, with a doc comment (1660-1670) describing precisely the raised scenario — a paste suspended at `navigator.clipboard.read()` resuming in its own closure on the captured TextEditor and bypassing the neutered `api.paste`. `disposed` is initialized false (text-editor.ts:369), set true as the first statement of `TextEditor.dispose()` (6081), never reset, and `EditorAPI.dispose()` invokes `textEditor?.dispose()` (editor.ts:4486). Both resuming write sites in `api.paste` — the rich path (editor.ts:4018) and the `readText()` fallback (editor.ts:4026) — funnel through that guarded method, and `textEditor` is a real `TextEditor` (editor.ts:2519), so the guard at 1671 is the code actually executed. The reviewer's proposed fix ("check `this.disposed` in `pasteContent`") is already in place, so no stale paste can land CRDT content after disposal via this path.

finding.summary: Disposal-based revocation is incomplete: `getStore()`/`getDoc()` still hand out live writable handles after `dispose()`, so a stale holder can write around `MUTATING_METHODS`
finding.evidence: `dispose()` now asserts "a write from a stale holder must not land" and "every mutating method has been neutered", and `isDisposed`'s doc says a disposed editor "is inert". Neither holds for the two accessors that return live handles: under `readOnly` they are backed by `readOnlyDocStore` (the split is documented at editor.ts:4505), but under disposal nothing wraps them — `getStore: () => (readOnly ? readStore : pageSetupGuardedStore)` and `getDoc: () => doc` are untouched by `neuterMutations`. Writes through those handles bypass the allowlist entirely: `docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68` captures `editor.getDoc()` and `editor.getStore().snapshot()` into `FindReplaceState`, and `handleReplace`/`handleReplaceAll` (docs-find-bar.tsx:132-148) mutate the Doc directly — its own comment at line 26-32 states this path is *not* covered by `MUTATING_METHODS`. That path happens to be saved today only by the separate `readOnly` prop gate at line 134/143, which is a different mechanism from disposal; any holder of `getStore()`/`getDoc()` that resumes after an await has no such gate. I could not point at a confirmed in-tree async caller, hence medium confidence, but the invariant the delta introduces is not actually enforced.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that at disposal "nothing wraps" the two live handles, so writes through them bypass revocation — is not what the code does. Both handles are built over a revocable wrapper at construction, keyed on the very flag dispose() sets. editor.ts:1138-1140 creates `revocableStore = revocableDocStore(docStore, () => disposed)`, uses it as `readStore` for non-readOnly mounts, and constructs the single `Doc` over it (so `getDoc()` at :3338 returns a Doc whose store is revocable). `getStore()` at :3339 returns `pageSetupGuardedStore`, which is a Proxy whose target is `revocableStore` (:3309), and whose one non-forwarded member also writes via `revocableStore` (:3307). read-only.ts:190-228 shows `revocableDocStore` consults `isRevoked()` on every property resolution (:197) and, once revoked, resolves members off `readOnlyDocStore`, where every non-reader is a no-op (read-only.ts:96-117) and set/defineProperty/deleteProperty/setPrototypeOf refuse (:209-216). dispose() sets `disposed = true` (editor.ts:4475) before neuterMutations, so handles captured earlier go dead immediately. Doc delegates each mutator per call to `this.store` (document.ts:98-106, 288-308), so no live function is retained. The cited find-bar path is covered by the same mechanism: docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68 captures the Doc/store, and find-replace.ts:59,71,79,83 route replaces through `this.doc.deleteText/insertText` → revocableStore → no-ops after disposal. Absence from MUTATING_METHODS is the documented, deliberate split (editor.ts:1128-1137, 3333-3337, 4535-4543), not a hole.
